title: Rust: Variables and Mutability
description: Declare variables using let, mut, and const in Rust.

steps.title: Immutable Variable
steps.description: Declare an immutable variable `name` with value `"Rust"` using `let` and print it.
hints: Immutable means you can't change it after assignment.

verification.failureMessage: Declare name with let and print it.

steps.title: Mutable Variable
steps.description: Declare a mutable variable `count` with `let mut`, set it to `5`, change it to `10`, and print it.
hints: The `mut` keyword makes the variable mutable.

verification.failureMessage: Use let mut to declare count, change it to 10, and print it.

steps.title: Type Annotations
steps.description: Declare variables with explicit type annotations: `x: i32 = 10` and `y: f64 = 3.14`. Print both.

verification.failureMessage: Declare x: i32 = 10 and y: f64 = 3.14 and print both.

steps.title: Constants with const
steps.description: Declare a constant `MAX_SPEED` with value `120` using `const` and print it.
hints: Constants must have explicit type annotations.
Constants are always immutable and can be declared at global scope.

verification.failureMessage: Use const to declare MAX_SPEED = 120 and print it.

steps.title: Variable Shadowing
steps.description: Use shadowing to declare a variable `x` as `5`, then shadow it as `"five"` (change type). Print both values.
hints: `let x = 5;` then `let x = "five";` creates a new variable that shadows the old one.
Shadowing lets you reuse the name with a different type.
Print `x` after each declaration to see both values.

verification.failureMessage: Print x after each shadowing to see '5' and 'five'.
